To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the biological effect of impulse processes is determined to a great extent by the parameters of the process itself (duration, intensity, and frequency) and to some extent by the parameters characterizing the individual's reaction to this process (the individual's susceptibility).

the hygienic estimation of the effect of impulse noise and vibration is to be based on the parameters of the mechanical action of the process on the body of the man, i.e. the acceleration, and on the acoustic parameters of the sound pressure level.
the biological effect of an impulse process is a result of the combined action of the physical parameters of this process, and that the biological effect depends on the duration of the process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of the biological effect of the impulse processes and the ways for their hygienic standardisation.
the following problems.

the following questions: 1) what physical parameters are responsible for the unfavourable effect on the human body of the impulse noise and vibrations? 2) what are the criteria of the hygienic estimation of the biological effect of impulse processes? 3) how should the hygienic standards be formulated in the case of the impulse processes?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

impulse noise and vibration are characterized by the following parameters: 1. Intensity (pressure, acceleration); 2. Frequency of the process; 3. Time of action (duration); 4. Repetition rate (frequency of impulses

the biological effect of impulse noise and vibration depends not only on the level and duration of their action, but also on the frequency of their repetition, and that this fact should be taken into account in the hygienic estimation of these processes.

the biological effect of impulse noise and vibration should be estimated and standardized in the first place with regard to the physical parameters which are the most important for the biological effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most adequate parameters for the standardization of impulse mechanical and acoustic processes are the maximum and the average values of the acceleration of vibration, the maximum and the peak values of sound pressure.

the hygienic standards of impulse noise and vibration are based on the physical parameters of the processes, which are responsible for the greatest degree of biological effect, and on the parameters of biological effect of the processes, i.e., on the data of the medico-biological investigations.

, as a result of the analysis of the literature and of the results of our own experiments, the most adequate physical parameters for the biological effect of impulse noise and vibration are: for noise, the peak sound pressure level and the peak sound exposure level; for mechanical vibration, the maximum acceleration, the maximum velocity and the maximum displacement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biological effects of impulse processes depend on the physical properties of these processes.
the biological effect of the impulse mechanical and acoustic processes is determined by the parameters that characterize the action on the body as a whole.
the most adequate parameter for hygienic standardizing impulse noise is the maximum sound pressure level (SPL) in the octave bands, and for vibration it is the maximum acceleration level (Amax).
